correctness.rationale: Direct same-model execution of standard-library verify.py rebuilds all 112827 nonempty simplices of the explicitly specified 20-vertex, 30-edge graph; gives face vector (30,375,2540,10155,24485,34930,27765,10890,1625,32); exhaustively topologically sorts 677415 reversed-gradient incidence arrows; leaves critical cells 0:1,4:1,5:25,6:86; computes signed Morse d5 and d6; verifies d5[0,5]=-1, d5*d6=0 and determinant +1 of specified 24x24 d6 minor. The high-dimensional CW model permits integral homotopy cancellation of one 4/5 pair and twenty-four 5/6 pairs, yielding sixty-two S6 cells. No finite sampling or unverified computational assumption is used.

originality.rationale: Searches for the precise ordinary matching complex of Isaacs J5, its line-graph independence-complex formulation, and 62 degree-six sphere decomposition located no identical or theorem-dominating statement. The historically definitive construction studies edge colouring, Brinkmann et al. study snark graph parameters, Bayer et al. prove a different restricted graph-family theorem. Indexed classifications of the dodecahedral and Desargues graph matching complexes have different graph arguments and distinct homotopy outcomes. The conclusion is best-knowledge originality, not uniqueness certified by a database partition.
residual_risks: Semantic published-finding corpus search is not a proof of exhaustive uniqueness; an unindexed or differently named equivalent computation may exist.
The Desargues and dodecahedral indexed result pages could not be read in full; their indexed statements, however, involve different graph objects with no evident encompassing theorem.
The search of literature and web resources is selective, though the original construction and the closest accessible general matching-complex paper were inspected materially.

value.rationale: J5 is the first nontrivial member of Isaacs’ canonical infinite family of cubic edge-uncolorable snarks. Its ordinary matching complex is a natural 30-vertex simplicial invariant whose complete homotopy type was not implied by graph matchings, edge-colouring results or general restricted-family matching-complex theorems. The pure 62-dimensional rank in degree six contrasts sharply with the mixed degree-five/six topology of two other natural cubic graphs with twenty vertices, offering a motivated reference point for comparing snark and non-snark matching topology. It remains a single-graph result, not a general snark theorem.
